subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should OpenClaw recommend Slack HTTP Request URLs over Socket Mode for hosted or public-ingress deployments to reduce reply latency, and where should that recommendation surface?
rationale: Current code already supports both transports; choosing stronger docs/setup guidance is a product and operator-experience decision, and the issue has protected maintainer/product-decision labels.

options.title: Recommend HTTP for hosted deployments
options.body: Update Slack setup and config guidance to say hosted/public-ingress gateways should prefer HTTP Request URLs for lower transport latency while keeping Socket Mode for local or no-ingress deployments.

options.title: Keep neutral transport guidance
options.body: Leave the docs focused on deployment shape and accept that Socket Mode users may continue to see the measured delivery gap.

options.title: Change setup defaults
options.body: Make setup flows steer eligible hosted deployments toward HTTP mode, which needs more upgrade and operator proof than a docs-only recommendation.

recommendation.title: Recommend HTTP for hosted deployments
recommendation.body: Update Slack setup and config guidance to say hosted/public-ingress gateways should prefer HTTP Request URLs for lower transport latency while keeping Socket Mode for local or no-ingress deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: Current Slack transport docs and provider-mode handling route most directly through this recent area history.
